note: P6-04d2c: merge the u and v division scratch into one allocation. P0 = eaf8a04d, P1 = d6cb67e2 on branch wip/p6-04d2c-scratch-merge.
verdict: a hard gate is violated. Every direct-core shape improves with no regressions, and the JS-level 8x4 shapes gain 29-31% -- mod_8x4 reaches 1.09x of pinned QuickJS -- but div_16x8 regresses 8.8% at the JS level with all sixteen combinations above 1.0, against an explicit gate that 16x8 and 24x8 must not regress by 1% or more.
plan_number_correction: the plan framed this as 4 -> 3 allocations, which was the pre-d2b topology. d2b already took multi-limb to 3, so this cut is 3 -> 2. The `both` path goes 4 -> 3.

mechanism.change: one [u][v] block replaces two allocations; u and v have identical lifetimes
mechanism.order_preserved: [u][v], matching what the two separate allocations produced logically, so the multiply-subtract window, the copies and the unshift all see the same relative layout
mechanism.alias_guard: a debug assertion pins that u and v are adjacent and disjoint, checking the u-end / v-start seam explicitly, since every helper below takes u's window and v as separate slices
mechanism.untouched: algorithm, estimate, reciprocal, correction, add-back, multiply-subtract, normalization, sign, result construction

topology.oom_sweep_now_a_topology_lock: the allocation count assertion is exact rather than a lower bound: three for both, two for div and rem

purity: identical counters on both corpora: digits 320754 / corrections 95009 / addbacks 0 / clamps 0 / submul limbs 2241550 and, on the frozen vectors, 10192 / 2939 / 24 / 8 / 35512, plus identical estimate-kind counts

direct_core.harness: four build instances per side, all sixteen combinations, three interleaved rounds
direct_core.summary: no regression anywhere; div_8x4 -6.7%, mod_8x4 -9.2%, 16x8 -2.2/-3.5%, 24x8 -1.1/-1.8%, one-digit shapes -6 to -18%
direct_core.one_stable_but_sub_gate_item: div-size-8x1 is 1.0066 with all sixteen combinations above 1.0, a stable +0.66% -- under the 1% line

div_8x4.reading: the merge removes a churning size class entirely, which is the 30.8% gain

div_16x8.reading: the merge introduces a churning class: the merged 25-limb block lands in a class the runtime does not keep populated, so the backing allocator is hit where P0 never hit it

size_class_mechanism.why_it_cuts_both_ways: P6-04d2.5 predicted exactly this fork: merging removes a touched size class on some shapes and adds one on others, and the slab returns an arena the moment a class empties. The same mechanism is worth 30% on one shape and costs 9% on another.

gates.div_8x4_or_mod_8x4_at_least_5_percent: met by a wide margin: direct-core 6.7% and 9.2%, JS 30.8% and 28.7%
gates.16x8_and_24x8_no_stable_regression: VIOLATED at the JS level: div_16x8 +8.8%, all sixteen combinations above 1.0, range 1.0850 to 1.0916. direct-core shows no regression (-2.2%), so this is purely a slab size-class effect.
gates.single_limb_and_sentinels_no_new_regress: met: div-size-8x1 +0.66% is stable but under 1%; mod-size-2x1 0.9908 and div-size-6x4 0.9275 both improve

options_for_adjudication.cost: loses mod_8x4 1.53x -> 1.09x and div_8x4 2.68x -> 1.86x, the largest remaining wins in the division line
div_16x8 goes 1.32x -> 1.44x, a named sentinel regressing against an explicit hard gate
options_for_adjudication.benefit: three of four JS cases improve, two of them dramatically; net across the four is strongly positive

options_for_adjudication.description: choose whether to merge based on the resulting size class, or pad the merged block into a class the runtime keeps populated
options_for_adjudication.note: this is allocator-aware tuning, which the plan explicitly excluded from d2c, so it would have to be its own cut

recommendation: adjudication is the user's. The measurement is unambiguous in both directions and the mechanism is confirmed, so the choice is a value judgement between a 30% gain on the shape the whole d2 sequence targeted and a 9% regression on a shape already inside 2x.

correctness.force_gc_cross_engine: the 20000-case differential is byte-identical to qjs under force-GC

limits: the size-class explanation comes from symbol shares plus the appearance and disappearance of addArena and _int_malloc; arena creations were not counted directly
24x8 has no JS case, so its JS behaviour under the merge is unmeasured -- only direct-core, where it improves 1.1 to 1.8%
no attempt was made to pick a friendlier size class, since that is allocator-aware tuning the plan excluded
only shift == 0 operands in the topology counts
